newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees violence against women in S. Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees violence against women in S. Korea.

text.p: Violence against women, especially rape, is a serious problem in South Korea, the United States said on Thursday.

"Women continued to face legal and societal discrimination. Violence against women and physical abuse remain serious problems," the State Department said in its annual human rights report of countries worldwide.

The department said some women's rights groups maintain that such violence has worsened in the past few years. Rape is described as a "serious problem" that is underreported because of the stigma of the crime. Some 6,173 cases were reported in 1994, the last year statistics were available.
"The law does not provide adequate protection to victims of abuse," the department concluded.

The report discusses how "key worker rights provisions were either delayed or deleted" from labour laws amended in December in an effort to meet internaitonal standards for worker rights while pro-management labour changes were enacted.
But the analysis appears more clinical than judgmental. The amended laws encountered strong opposition, protests and strikes by Korean labour organisations.
